settings.name_in_paper: Graphical multi-armed bandit (contextual bandit with payoff decomposition over an interaction graph)
unmapped: Actions and contexts are joint assignments to discrete variables; expected payoff F decomposes as a sum of unknown potential functions over known variable subsets P (known interaction graph)
Contexts chosen arbitrarily by Nature (arbitrary sequence), payoffs stochastic given context-action pair
settings.definition_quote: In each round t = 1, ..., T: 1. Nature chooses an arbitrary joint context assignment x^t_C, which is observed by the learning algorithm. 2. The learning algorithm chooses a joint action assignment x^t_A. 3. The learning algorithm receives an independent random payoff f^t in [0,1] with expectation F(x^t_A, x^t_C). ... Assumption 1 (Payoff Decomposition). We are given a collection of variable subsets P such that the unknown expected payoff function F has the form F(x) = sum_{P} f_P(x_P)

algorithms.name: GraphicalBandits (BestAct + PayEst with KWIK linear regression)

symbols.d_rank: rank of the coefficient matrix M (paper's d)
symbols.w: treewidth of the tree decomposition of the action subgraph
symbols.m_dom: maximum number of values of a variable, max_i |X_i| (paper's m)
symbols.E_card: number of edges |E| of the tree decomposition

conditions: Expected payoff decomposes according to known collection P (Assumption 1)
A tree decomposition of the action subgraph with treewidth w is given
tuning: PayEst = KWIK linear regression of Cesa-Bianchi et al. (2009) with parameters eps, delta

source.quote: Let d = rank(M) be the rank of the coefficient matrix, and let T = (A, E) be the tree decomposition of the action subgraph GA with treewidth w. The regret R(T) of GraphicalBandits after T rounds is at most R(T) ≤ O(dw/ε² log(T m|E|/εδ) + 2|A|εT + δT) and the computational complexity of each round is O(m^{2w}|E|).

results.notes: Regret defined as expectation of sum of max F - F(x_t), i.e. pseudo-regret against best action per context. Per-round compute O(m^{2w}|E|): polynomial only for constant treewidth. Horizon: eps, delta are fixed parameters; T not required by algorithm here, but recorded as known for consistency with the setting. Text extracted from PDF; expression reconstructed.
